title: [Performance] Avoid redundant Engram lookup output initialization
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Engram preparation zero-initializes a local BF16 result that lookup immediately overwrites. Allocate it with `torch.empty` instead, removing one redundant full-result initialization per prepared layer. Both native device-table and mapped-host kernels write every allocated local head, including zeroes for invalid IDs; the CPU reference has the same contract. Empty-token/empty-head tensors contain no elements to initialize.

This follow-up comes from the Engram data-path investigations in #16689 and #19528. Credit to both efforts for motivating the removal of intermediate buffer work: this patch applies their final-buffer/overwrite reasoning to the existing common embedding path. It is independent of their VMM/shared-owner changes and can merge on its own.

DP row exchange, TP head all-gather, graph-buffer publication, and tail padding are unchanged.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Lower local Engram preparation overhead, with no API/configuration or numerical change. A performance release-note fragment is included.

### How was this patch tested?

- Added 24 parameterized dirty-buffer correctness cases for BF16/INT8, TP-shaped heads 1/2/4, DP windows 1/2, zero/nonzero tokens, non-contiguous layer IDs, and valid/invalid IDs. Newly allocated output is poisoned with NaNs and checked before mocked collectives and at return.
- Executed those cases locally using isolated production `embed_gathered`, `lookup`, and CPU-reference source, because local vLLM is unavailable. This bypasses package imports and mocks collectives; it is not a native full-suite pytest run. In a normal test environment: `pytest tests/ut/models/test_engram.py -k lookup_overwrites_dirty_output_before_exchange`.
- A3 NPU: 24 HBM/local-host-VMM workload shapes passed native INT8 lookup versus CPU reference and graph-replay before/after equality. The benchmark used the existing image's native lookup wrappers/kernels and the modified preparation method; it was not a full wheel built from this branch.
- `bash format.sh ci` and `git diff --check`.

Matched NPU microbenchmark, microseconds per layer preparation:

| Backing | Local heads | Tokens | zeros | empty | Time reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| HBM | 6 | 32 | 13.663 | 11.560 | 15.39% |
| HBM | 12 | 32 | 13.370 | 10.177 | 23.88% |
| HBM | 12 | 4096 | 197.403 | 182.265 | 7.67% |
| Local host VMM | 6 | 32 | 14.933 | 12.766 | 14.51% |
| Local host VMM | 12 | 32 | 14.778 | 12.238 | 17.19% |
| Local host VMM | 12 | 4096 | 403.760 | 392.944 | 2.68% |

Method: 65,536 fully initialized rows, 256 INT8 codes + 8 FP32 scales per row, eight distinct seeded query batches per NPUGraph. Baseline/candidate differ only in the output allocator. Three warmup replays, ABBA timing phases (each >=0.2 s and >=20 samples); pooled NPU-event median divided by eight calls. Tokens 32/128/1024/4096 and local heads 6/12/24 were tested for both backings. The method's ID-contiguity copy remains in both variants.

These are warm, single-NPU preparation timings. `tp_size=dp_size=1` intentionally isolates allocation/initialization plus lookup; head counts represent local shard sizes, not actual TP/DP execution. It does not measure TP collectives, graph-buffer publication/padding, remote HCCS reads, full-model E2E throughput, or a hardware bandwidth ceiling. The local VMM setup used the adapter from #19528; the optimization itself needs no VMM support. No E2E speedup is claimed.

### Checklist

- [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage: zero/nonzero tokens and invalid IDs.
- [x] Meaningful tests: dirty outputs must be completely overwritten before communication.
- [x] Performance evidence attached with measurement boundaries.
- [ ] Native multi-rank TP2/4 and full-model E2E validation for this patch.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c0b6f74bee518aeaf5d72b200a0216e72fbb5e7c
